title: Actual HanLP and GLiNER lane/coalescer lifecycle controls
question: Do actual CPU provider lanes preserve a useful coalesced sibling after one borrower stops, drain on operation cancellation, report owned-child crashes, and isolate static/native GLiNER member refusals?
method: Use actual ProviderExecution and native HanLP/GLiNER children. Controlled reply-read gates run after the native request is sent (GLiNER admission first completes), then stop one running borrower, cancel the operation or SIGKILL only the captured owned native child. Independently inspect survivor context/correlation, original or reduced batch ordinals, refusal, byte retirement and actual joined/closed child ownership. Test32769byte GLiNER early refusal and600word native-preparation refusal alongside a useful sibling. Custody refresh: root formatting and safe source cleanup preserve probe parameters and assertions. Native execution predates the later lazy-admission repair; the coordinator judges native worker, lane exchange and coalescer semantics unchanged. These receipts qualify their stated native batch/projection/lifecycle questions, not the final scheduler's pre-hydration admission timing, retention or DB fencing. Final integrated native checks are separately coordinator-owned.
